abstract: KATP channels composed of sulfonylurea receptor 1 (SUR1) and Kir6.2 encoded by ABCC8 and KCNJ11, respectively, play a crucial role in regulating insulin secretion. Nonsense mutations that introduce premature termination codons (PTCs) in ABCC8 and KCNJ11 disrupt KATP channel expression, resulting in congenital hyperinsulinism (HI). Currently, there is no effective non-invasive treatment for HI caused by KATP-PTCs. Anticodon-edited transfer RNAs (ACE-tRNAs), which suppress PTCs and restore full-length protein expression, have emerged as potential therapies for diseases caused by nonsense mutations. Here, we evaluate the efficacy of ACE-tRNAs to rescue the expression and function of KATP-PTCs in a heterologous COS cell expression system. In five selected SUR1-PTCs, ACE-tRNAs incorporating native amino acids at the PTC sites recovered KATP channel expression and activity. ACE-tRNALeuUGA, a highly efficient suppressor incorporating leucine at PTCs, also rescued protein expression of all five variants; however, two of the five rescued PTC variants showed impaired gating, indicating functional intolerance to Leu substitution at these positions. An exhaustive screen of the rescue effects of ACE-tRNALeu on 100 HI-associated KATP-PTCs reported to date demonstrated therapeutically meaningful functional rescue of 60 out of 92 SUR1-PTC variants and 6 out of 8 Kir6.2-PTC variants. In addition, optimized ACE-tRNASer rescues several PTCs that were unresponsive to ACE-tRNALeu, further expanding the applicability of ACE-tRNA for rescuing PTC variants. Our results demonstrate that ACE-tRNAs are effective in rescuing the expression and function of a majority of KATP PTC variants and suggest ACE-tRNAs as a promising molecular therapy for HI caused by nonsense mutations.
